item.title: SpaceX Boosts the A.I. Rally
item.description: Tech stocks are up after the rocket and artificial intelligence company beat earnings estimates — and Elon Musk confirmed it is weighing a deal with Tesla.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe and Sri Muppidi
item.media:credit: Andres Kudacki for The New York Times
item.media:description: Elon Musk’s company SpaceX reported stellar results, bolstering the artificial intelligence stock rally.

item.title: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
item.description: A deal would consolidate Elon Musk’s holdings in rockets, cars and artificial intelligence into a company worth well over $3 trillion.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac and Jack Ewing
item.media:description: SpaceX’s blockbuster public offering on the Nasdaq in June helped make Elon Musk, who is also the chief executive of Tesla, the first person to be worth more than a trillion dollars.

item.title: Senator Asks 4 Accounting Giants to Describe Malta Tax Advice
item.description: Ron Wyden, ranking Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, is investigating the firms over their role in helping corporations dodge billions in taxes.
item.dc:creator: Jesse Drucker
item.media:description: Senator Ron Wyden, Democrat of Oregon, wrote in a letter that “tax lawyers are devising clever strategies for corporate giants to continue exploiting offshore tax havens to avoid paying their fair share.”

item.title: A Battle for Control of India’s Biggest Business Empire
item.description: A boardroom fight, an attempted veto and government intervention have plunged the Tata Group, one of India’s most revered institutions, into a fight over its future.
item.dc:creator: Alex Travelli
item.media:credit: Shubhadeep Mukherjee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Natarajan Chandrasekaran, chairman of the Tata Sons holding company, at Bombay House, its headquarters. The hallway entrance features a stone sculpture of the company's founder, Jamsetji Tata.

item.title: For an Experiment in Political Affirmative Action, Look to Taiwan
item.description: The island adopted quotas for women running for public office decades before other countries. The upshot? Today, few of them need quotas to get elected.
item.dc:creator: Li Yuan
item.media:credit: Lam Yik Fei for The New York Times
item.media:description: Su Chiao-hui campaigning for a mayoral post in Taiwan. Women hold 42 percent of Taiwan’s legislative seats, the highest share in Asia and comparable to Nordic countries.

item.title: U.K. Approves Long-Stalled Jackdaw Gas Drilling Project in the North Sea
item.description: The project will lessen the country’s dependence on imported energy, though environmental advocates say it undercuts a pledge to reduce carbon emissions.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman
item.media:description: Oil rigs on the northeast coast of Scotland.

item.title: Britain Is Said to Approve New Gas Drilling in the North Sea
item.description: Jackdaw, a natural gas field off the coast of Scotland, would be the first new gas extraction project in the North Sea since a government moratorium in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman
item.media:description: An oil rig off the northeast coast of Scotland.

item.title: SpaceX Swings to a Profit, as A.I. Business Grows
item.description: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its artificial intelligence spending had soared, but revenue more than doubled from its Starlink internet satellite service and A.I. products.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac and Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Andres Kudacki for The New York Times
item.media:description: SpaceX’s performance on the stock market is a barometer for Anthropic, the A.I. company that may go public as early as next month.

item.title: Netflix Is Great at Making Money. Its Problem Is Keeping Viewers Hooked.
item.description: The streaming service reported a 12 percent increase in quarterly revenue, but acknowledged that stagnant viewership, particularly in the U.S. and Canada, was a major concern.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Sperling
item.media:description: Despite being the most-watched paid streaming service in the world, Netflix is not growing fast enough for its top executives or its shareholders.

item.title: Boeing’s Large 737 Max Jet Secures U.S. Approval
item.description: After years of delay, the Federal Aviation Administration certified the 737 Max 10, the largest version of Boeing’s most popular plane.
item.dc:creator: Niraj Chokshi
item.category: Boeing 737 Max Groundings and Safety Concerns (2019)
item.media:description: A Boeing 737 Max 10 in production at the company’s factory in Everett, Wash., in July.

item.title: Heading to France? Amid Recent Unrest, Here’s What to Know
item.description: Rioting over affordability and public education has swept through Paris and other French cities, and there may be more to come.
item.dc:creator: Ceylan Yeğinsu and Tariro Mzezewa
item.media:description: On Monday, protesters blocked the entrance to the Louvre museum in Paris. The demonstrations in support of public education and the cost of living were held in several French cities, including Marseille, Lille and Nice.

item.title: Trump Tariffs on Canada Spark Latest Lawsuit Over Trade Powers
item.description: Once again, the president’s ability to wage a trade war without Congress will come before a court that has repeatedly ruled against him.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm
item.media:description: The fate of President Trump’s tariffs now rests in the hands of the Court of International Trade.

item.title: A ‘Doom Loop’ Threatens France as Populism Confronts Markets
item.description: The turmoil shows the profound challenges facing governments stuck between unhappy citizens and wary bond investors.
item.dc:creator: Eshe Nelson and Jim Tankersley
item.media:description: Police officers during civil unrest in Paris on Sunday.

item.title: Investors in Anticipation Over Musk’s Next Big SpaceX Deal
item.description: Ahead of SpaceX’s quarterly earnings report, many on Wall Street are wondering whether Elon Musk will combine it with Tesla.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe, Sri Muppidi and Vivienne Walt
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Investors and analysts will probably press Elon Musk, left, about SpaceX’s spending on artificial intelligence — and whether he might seek to combine the company with Tesla.

item.title: Trump Announces $8 Billion Plan to Cover Farm Losses
item.description: Under the Harvest Fuel Relief Program, the Agriculture Department will provide economic aid for farmers hurt by high diesel prices.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Draper
item.media:description: President Trump held a rally on Monday night in Kansas, where farmers traditionally form a solid Republican voting bloc.

item.title: Knicks Ticket Prices Are Soaring After Last Season’s Championship
item.description: Knicks tickets have never been cheap, but prices for the first game alone are soaring after last season’s championship — more than a trip to Paris.
item.dc:creator: Tania Ganguli
item.media:credit: Vincent Alban for The New York Times
item.media:description: Game 4 of the N.B.A. finals between the New York Knicks and the San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden in June.

item.title: How Do Airports Prepare for a Plane Crash? Go Inside JFK’s Disaster Drill.
item.description: U.S. airports are required to hold a full-scale disaster drill every three years. Go inside a simulated plane crash at Kennedy Airport last weekend.
item.dc:creator: Gabe Castro-Root and Lexi Parra
item.category: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
item.media:description: Emergency workers attended to a volunteer playing a victim of a simulated plane crash during a drill at Kennedy Airport on Saturday.

item.title: Christiane Amanpour Says She Is Leaving CNN After 43 Years
item.description: The chief international anchor, one of the most famous names in broadcast news, started as an assistant at the network in 1983.
item.dc:creator: Michael M. Grynbaum
item.media:credit: Vincent Tullo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Christiane Amanpour, CNN’s chief international anchor, is departing the network next June.

item.title: Jon Stewart to Stay at ‘The Daily Show’ Through the 2028 Election
item.description: Ratings have surged since Mr. Stewart returned over two years ago to host the show on Monday nights.
item.dc:creator: John Koblin
item.category: Late Show with Stephen Colbert (TV Program)
The Daily Show with Jon Stewart (TV Program)
item.media:credit: Matt Wilson/Comedy Central, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Jon Stewart’s two-year deal is a shot in the arm for the late-night-show genre, where cancellations have been piling up.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Postpones Its FII Investment Event After Houthi Attacks
item.description: The Future Investment Initiative, a centerpiece of Saudi efforts to diversify its economy from its reliance on the energy industry, was set to begin next week.
item.dc:creator: Humza Jilani
item.media:description: The opening ceremony of the Future Investment Initiative, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, last year.

item.title: Black Unemployment Hints at a Job Market in Worse Shape Than It Seems
item.description: The Black unemployment rate climbed a percentage point to 7 percent in September, almost double the rate for white workers.
item.dc:creator: Talmon Joseph Smith
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gena Pemberton has not had a full-time job since July 2025, when her role as chief inclusion and impact officer at Omnicom Health was eliminated.

item.title: Gilbert Bigio, Haitian Tycoon Linked to Gangs, Dies at 91
item.description: Reportedly the wealthiest man in the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere, Gilbert Bigio was sanctioned for ties to criminal gangs. He was 91.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nossiter

item.title: At Victoria’s Secret’s 2026 Fashion Show, an Old Stereotype of Sexy
item.description: The angels were out in full force on the runway, including Kylie Jenner and both Hadids. So were the wings.
item.dc:creator: Vanessa Friedman
item.media:description: Kylie Jenner in the Victoria’s Secret diamond Fantasy Bra by Jacob & Co.

item.title: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
item.description: Anthropic, an A.I. rival to SpaceX, earlier said it would form a “public benefit fund” and other tech moguls have contributed to savings accounts for children.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac
item.media:description: Elon Musk said he would give one share of SpaceX stock to every child in America, but did not specify how.

item.title: Anthropic’s I.P.O. Charity
item.description: The artificial intelligence giant plans to contribute 5 percent of its stock into a philanthropic fund. But its generosity depends on the A.I. boom continuing.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe, Sri Muppidi and Ian Mount
item.media:description: Anthropic has announced plans to give 5 percent of its shares to a new charitable fund as it moves closer to an I.P.O.

item.title: Art Basel Las Vegas? The Fight Over Miami Beach’s Fair
item.description: After 18 months of negotiations and warnings that it might relocate to Nevada, the Art Basel fair will remain in Miami Beach through 2031.
item.dc:creator: Brett Sokol
item.media:description: Throngs of visitors to the opening of Art Basel Miami Beach last December at the Miami Beach Convention Center. After a vote last week, the fair’s new contract offers five more years and veto power over competing art events.

item.title: ‘A Ticking Time Bomb’: An Economic Crisis Looms in Indonesia
item.description: Once a model of economic stability, Indonesia now faces growing hardship at home as President Prabowo Subianto’s policies shake investor confidence.
item.dc:creator: Sui-Lee Wee and Rin Hindryati
item.media:credit: Ulet Ifansasti for The New York Times
item.media:description: Commuters during the morning rush hour in Jakarta. A vulnerable middle class has continued to shrink.

item.title: U.S. Political Money Funnels to Indian Bots to Lure Voters
item.description: At least three dozen videos of people on the street expressing support for a Democratic candidate appeared millions of times on social media. It was unclear who paid for them.
item.dc:creator: Steven Lee Myers
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times; Nic Antaya for The New York Times

item.title: The VW Bus, Now Electrified, Keeps on Truckin’
item.description: A restored version of Volkswagen’s Flower Power-era Microbus, kitted out by Kindred Motorworks, is aiming for the affluent, while VW’s own E.V. is slow to get moving, much like its forebear.
item.dc:creator: Jim Motavalli
item.media:description: The 23-window Microbus, in its original form, had less than 60 horsepower. The “restomod” version from Kindred Motorworks swaps in a much more capable electric system.

item.title: Strong Exports Stabilize China’s Economic Growth in Official Statistics
item.description: A prolonged housing crash, sluggish consumer spending and plunging investment have left China dependent on exports to keep the economy growing.
item.dc:creator: Keith Bradsher
item.media:credit: Gilles Sabrié for The New York Times
item.media:description: A mall in Beijing. China’s domestic economy, particularly retail sales, struggled in the third quarter.

item.title: Elizabeth Holmes Documentary ‘You Can See Everything’ Opens to Over 2,000 Sold-Out Shows
item.description: “You Can See Everything,” a documentary about the Theranos founder, made a big splash for a movie not yet in wide release. And Netflix had a box office milestone.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Sperling

item.title: 3 Charts That Explain the Economy as Voters Head to the Polls
item.description: Inflation is high, consumer spending is strong and seemingly everything depends on what happens with artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Ben Casselman

item.title: Oklahoma Families Faced the Hottest Summer Ever and an Electricity Crisis
item.description: Record heat and a rising demand for electricity are closing in on Oklahoma families trying to keep the lights on and the AC running.
item.dc:creator: Eli Saslow and Erin Schaff
item.media:description: Genia Weitz and her husband, Daryl Mason, confined themselves to their living room to try to keep their electricity bill down.

item.title: United’s C.E.O. Says It Should Cost More Not to Sit in the Middle Seat
item.description: Scott Kirby of United Airlines said that “it’s expensive to fly airplanes” and that airfares may have further to rise.
item.dc:creator: Jordyn Holman
item.media:credit: Lyndon French for The New York Times
item.media:description: After he was passed over for the top job at American Airlines, Scott Kirby said, he “wanted to go somewhere else and prove something.”

item.title: Trump Offers Putin Economic Relief in Hopes That Russia Will Return the Favor
item.description: The Trump administration is ignoring the will of Congress and waiving new Russia sanctions amid fears that high energy prices will cost Republicans in next month’s elections.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport

item.title: States Are Stepping Up as the New Antitrust Enforcers
item.description: With the Trump administration taking a relaxed approach, attorneys general around the country have ramped up their scrutiny of mergers.
item.dc:creator: Tamzin Booth
item.media:description: “When the federal administration has stepped back from enforcing our antitrust laws, state attorneys general have stepped up,” Letitia James, attorney general of New York, told DealBook.

item.title: The Reporter Who Exposed Elizabeth Holmes on Nathan Fielder’s Documentary
item.description: Ms. Holmes handed the makers of “You Can See Everything” — and the rest of the world — a microscope with which to observe and dissect her lies.

item.title: Corporate Tax Revenue Falls Even as Profits Soar Under Trump
item.description: The annual decline was about $70 billion. Companies are writing off billions in A.I. investments, taking advantage of tax cuts that President Trump signed into law.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:description: A law signed by President Trump last year lets companies claim larger deductions in the year they make new investments.

item.title: Can Cereal Be Healthy? Big Companies Are Trying.
item.description: As more Americans turn away from the snap, crackle and sugar, the industry is trying to capitalize on our current obsession with wellness.
item.dc:creator: Kim Severson
item.media:credit: Shawn Michael Jones for The New York Times
item.media:description: Since cereal was invented in 1863, its makers have repeatedly aimed to capitalize on the latest health fads and fixations.

item.title: It’s Time to Shop Medicare, and This Year, It’s Extra Important
item.description: Be sure to read your mail this fall — big changes to prescription drug plans and Medicare Advantage provider networks are coming, and could cost you more.
item.dc:creator: Mark Miller

item.title: Weak Links Start to Show in A.I. Borrowing
item.description: Debt trouble at CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank raises questions about whether there are broader problems with the data center build-out.
item.dc:creator: Maureen Farrell and Rob Copeland
item.media:credit: Ivan Pierre Aguirre for The New York Times
item.media:description: The site where Project Jupiter, an artificial intelligence data center, is under construction in Santa Teresa, N.M. Oracle is having trouble obtaining state permits for its energy needs.

item.title: M.L.B. Playoff Ads With Sydney Sweeney and Megan Fox Draw Backlash
item.description: Commercials promoting a gambling platform and endorsing male enhancement have rankled fans, and even athletes. Who is in charge?
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner
item.media:description: A billboard ad in Times Square for the sports-betting site Novig featuring the actress Sydney Sweeney. She appeared in commercials aired during the Major League Baseball playoffs.

item.title: Netflix Hurries to Rewrite Its Narrative With Layoffs and a Sudden Firing
item.description: Despite strong revenues and profits, the streaming service cut 1,000 jobs and jettisoned its chief content officer. Drops in the stock price and viewer engagement are to blame.
item.dc:creator: John Koblin and Nicole Sperling
item.media:credit: Aleksey Kondratyev for The New York Times
item.media:description: Netflix is replacing Bela Bajaria, the company’s chief content officer, with Peter Rice, a Fox and Disney veteran.

item.title: U.S. Budget Deficit Nears $2 Trillion, a Reality Check for Trump’s Cost Cutting
item.description: Higher interest rates are inflating borrowing costs as the Trump administration spends on the Iran war and tariff refunds.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport

item.title: You’ve Found a Long-Lost CD. Can You Still Get Your Money?
item.description: The bank was required to hold the certificate of deposit only for a limited time, and now has no record of the money. Experts offer tips to avoid having this happen to you.
item.dc:creator: Ann Carrns

item.title: When Will the Fed Move on Rates?
item.description: Kevin Warsh, the central bank’s chairman, suggested he wouldn’t push to raise borrowing rates this month. But persistent inflation may force the Fed’s hand.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe, Sri Muppidi and Ian Mount
item.media:description: Kevin Warsh’s nonanswer on interest rates is giving stock investors some comfort.

item.title: Indonesian Stocks Plunge as MSCI Threatens to Drop Market from Indexes
item.description: The potential downgrade by MSCI, an influential index provider, adds to a deepening crisis of investor confidence in the economic policies of President Prabowo Subianto.
item.dc:creator: Sui-Lee Wee
item.media:description: A display at the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta on Friday.

item.title: Feel Like You’re Overpaying for Hotels? Blame Expedia, a New Lawsuit Says.
item.description: The booking giant is accused of breaking federal antitrust laws and forcing millions of customers to overspend on stays by as much as 30 percent.
item.dc:creator: Ryley Ober
item.media:credit: Serene Lee/SOPA Images, via LightRocket, via Getty Images
item.media:description: If a hotel offered a lower price on a competing platform, the suit claims Expedia would make the hotel harder to find on the company’s platforms.

item.title: Lufthansa’s Final A346 Flight Marks the End of an Aviation Love Story
item.description: Lufthansa’s quirky plane, with its extra-long fuselage, four engines and restrooms down a flight of stairs, has a devoted following. Now, the carrier, one of few still flying the model, is taking it out of service.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Trunsky

item.title: Trump Hasn’t Lowered Drug Prices for These Voters
item.description: President Trump has been promoting his efforts to reduce drug prices, but many Americans have not seen relief from rising costs for prescriptions and insurance premiums.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Robbins
item.media:credit: David Lawrence for The New York Times
item.media:description: James Evans lives in Florida’s Seventh Congressional District, a fast-growing, Republican-leaning region northeast of Orlando, where the pain of rising health care costs is felt by a wide swath of voters.
